items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: even when I joined Fletcher Henderson at the Roseland Ballroom I was just 24 years old and in that band you had ... Fletcher at the piano

ctx.x: well then apparently he didn't learn it anywhere he had it

but it's in him yeah and but the average kid would say I don't want to play that I want to play uh uh uh uh I'm with you on that you know when I was a teenager I listened to the good old greats you know what I mean the boys around my crowd was gonna go to the next neighborhood and fight and all that you know what I mean so I thought they were stupid see I want to hear the elders of people and what they talked about in music and everything like that even when I joined Fletcher Henderson at the Roseland Ballroom I…
working with men that are better than you and I guess there was a time when there was someone better than you when you were awfully young.

items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: But that was when I went with Fletch Henderson, after I left Joe, 1924.

ctx.x: There were like one or two records, I think it was chimes, blues, or something like that. But I never wanted to do that in Oval Joe. Did you sing at all? No. That came later? Yeah. Because he knew I was singing, but the main thing was to kind of play with him. And I was singing in a little quartet and he knew all of that, you know.

Was there any vocalist with the band? No, no vocalist. But then you made records shortly after that. After that, yeah. With vocalists, with Bessie Smith. Yeah. But that was when I went with Fletch Henderson, after I left Joe, 1924. I thought we could play one of the records by Ma Rainey that you played on, as an example of the kind of blues of that period and the blues singers and the way in which you worked with them. This one is called Countin' the Blues by Ma Rainey with the accompaniment by Louis Armstrong,…

items.title: Louis Armstrong and Herman Chittison Interview, 1960-05-04
items.q: I became friends with him. You all played piano together? He would, yeah, that's right. He would, we'd have sessions.

ctx.x: and i'm afraid our time is all over

Neil, I was going through some books here that I wanted to ask you about, some early recordings and all, but before I did that, I wanted to ask you about some mundane facts about yourself, you know, about your birth date and where you were born and all that kind of stuff. I was born on the south side. Here in Atlanta? In Atlanta, Georgia. Native son. Yeah. On the Capitol Avenue. What was your part of you? Capitol Avenue? Near Capitol Avenue, the Creekmont Sanitarium. And that is considered a historic part of…

Well, now, Eddie, I live down in the alley. I live down in the alley. Well, I can't hear as I can be. Honey, I can be. Oh, my baby, I live down in the alley. That doesn't sound familiar to you. Well, now, Eddie, Eddie Haywood is on this label saying that he recorded with Sloppy Henry.
